taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: stems mostly erect, cylindric, (5-)10-40 x 4.5-8 cm.

traits.height_max_m.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 237, Echinocereus fasciculatus: stems 16-45 cm long.

traits.woodiness.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: fleshy stems, woody only in the core at the base, as the template's.

traits.rosette.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: stems ribbed and spiny, without leaves.

traits.stem_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 237, Echinocereus fasciculatus: stems green; mid green in the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.stem_diameter_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: stems (5-)10-40 x 4.5-8 cm.

traits.ribs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: ribs 10-15, crests slightly undulate.

traits.areole_spacing_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: areoles 10-15 mm apart.

traits.radial_spines.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: radial spines 7-15 per areole, 5-15 mm.

traits.radial_spine_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: radial spines 5-15 mm.

traits.central_spines.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: central spines 1-3 per areole, divergent-porrect, 15-75 mm, all terete; one main central and up to two more are drawn.

traits.central_spine_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: central spines 15-75 mm.

traits.central_spine_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: spines usually straight.

traits.spine_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: individual spines with broad zones of different colors: yellowish, reddish brown, or gray to black, or white to black, becoming gray; pale tan in the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.central_spine_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 237, Echinocereus fasciculatus: centrals pale with dark tips; radials whitish or greyish; sRGB by eye.

traits.spine_colour_aged.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: spines becoming gray; sRGB by eye.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: inner tepals rose-pink to magenta, with midstripes darker; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: flowers 6-10 x 8-10 cm.

traits.anther_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: anthers yellow.

traits.stigma_colour.note: Stigma lobes green, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 322317171, 40195026, 219261024, 266049792, 231226335, 214190215, 99942291, 153169686): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: fruits bright red or orange-red, 20-30 mm; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: fruits 20-30 mm.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: flowering Mar-Jun.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 p. 161, 164, 165 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Echinocereus fasciculatus: fruiting May-Jul.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for pinkflower hedgehog cactus from Flora of North America vol. 4 pp. 161-165: open clumps of 5-30 erect stems (stems 15, clump_radius 0.2), stems to 40 cm (height_max 0.4). Their girth comes from stem_diameter_max_m through the column's rule; growth rates and the flower ring are kept from the template, a close relative (FNA: once treated as E. engelmannii subsp. fasciculatus).

appearance.note: By eye from the photos (observations 322317171, 40195026, 219261024, 266049792, 231226335, 214190215, 99942291, 153169686): an open clump of green ribbed stems bristling with long, straight, pale tan spines, the main central longest and dark-tipped, large magenta flowers with a green stigma. Spine counts, lengths and colours and the ribs come from the traits through the family's rules; the main central is one of the 1 to 3 centrals FNA counts, and up to two more are set by hand.

allometry.note: 0.3 m tall at 20 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m), batch s1b (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles, Hitchcock and Flora of North America, counts and colours from photos.
